subject: Quantivis SLA exceptions & credit scenario planning
messages:
From: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@quantivis.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@quantivis.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial SLA ask — uptime + credit cap scenarios

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking the time on Friday. As we dig into the procurement checklist we wanted to surface a few specific SLA asks so we can map internal approvals. Attached is a short PDF that shows our target commitments and why the credit cap matters for legal/finance (quantivis_sla_request.pdf).

High-level asks:
- Uptime: we would like to see 99.95% for the primary region (us-west) for our production workload.
- Monthly service credit cap: we are asking for an upper bound of 9% of monthly invoice for any single month. Our legal team is uncomfortable with the standard open-ended / high-percent credits.
- Latency: p95 inference latency target of 220ms for standard text-generation endpoints.
- Maintenance carveouts: we can accept scheduled maintenance with a 72-hour notice, but need it limited to 4 hours/month for the production pool.

A few special asks: pro-rata credit calculation for partial-month migrations and a clearly defined exception path if we move to Dedicated or Private deployment mid-contract.

Can you sketch options (hosted baseline, committed spend + dedicated, private) with corresponding credit caps? We're trying to align procurement and legal next week.

Best,
Marta Gomez
Sr. Procurement Manager, Quantivis
M: +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: quantivis_sla_request.pdf (1 page summary)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 11:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA ask — uptime + credit cap scenarios

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear summary and the PDF. Looping in Aditya (account lead) and Marissa (contracts/ops) to help scope options.

Short answer: we can structure three realistic paths and the credit caps move with commitment and deployment model. Draft options below — I'll have Aditya follow up with concrete numbers and a short credit-scenario sheet.

Option A — Hosted (no committed spend)
- Baseline uptime: 99.9% (standard)
- Monthly credit cap: 30% (applies to standard hosted agreements)
- Latency: best-effort for p95; can allocate higher priority routing for an added fee
- Maintenance: standard 72-hour notice, 8 hours/month allowed

Option B — Committed Dedicated Pool (recommended for Quantivis)
- Baseline uptime: 99.95% for the dedicated pool (with a capacity commit and regional pin)
- Monthly credit cap: can be reduced to 6–9% depending on term (12/24 months) and spend commitment
- Latency: guaranteed p95 target with dedicated capacity and monitored SLOs
- Maintenance: we can limit planned maintenance to 4 hours/month with advanced notice and can schedule maintenance windows during low-traffic windows

Option C — Private deployment (on-prem / VPC)
- Baseline uptime: depends on customer infra; Redwood provides availability guidance and automation; SLA pass-through is negotiable
- Credit cap: typically lower as Redwood is not controlling infra; can be structured in carveouts

Next steps: Aditya will send a credit-scenario workbook with concrete example calculations (monthly invoice X => max credit Y) and a comparison of 12 vs 24 month terms. Marissa will send redline language for maintenance carveouts and the pro-rata calculation method we use. If Quantivis is open to a pilot of Dedicated, we can include a one-month trial period.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Soojin

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@quantivis.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA ask — legal/ops considerations and redline

Hi all — a few legal/ops clarifications to make sure Quantivis and we have the same expectations. I'm attaching a draft redline that covers the measurement window, maintenance carveouts, calculation method for credits, and an exception path for Dedicated -> Private transitions (redline_sla_qv_draft.docx).

Key points from our side:
- Measurement window: monthly availability measured as: (total seconds in window - cumulative outage seconds impacting >50% of your pinned pool)/total seconds. Outage detection requires corroborating traces and customer-reported incidents; we will use our incident timeline to compute overlap.
- Credit calculation: credits are pro-rata of that month's invoice computed as (minutes of qualifying downtime / total minutes in month) * monthly invoice, subject to the credit cap. We do not do daily prorata; we calculate with minute granularity.
- Partial-month migrations: we will apply the same minute-granular calculation; however, credits for the partial month are capped at the pro-rated cap for the days the dedicated pool was active unless otherwise negotiated.
- Carveouts: planned maintenance (with 72h notice) and force majeure events are excluded. We will agree in the SLO appendix a definition of "planned" vs "urgent" maintenance.
- Observability: for a reduced credit cap we require token-level tracing for the pinned pool for a 90-day validation window (logs retained per our standard retention unless you purchase extended retention).

If Quantivis accepts the observability requirements and a 12-month commit, we can reduce the credit cap to 6% and guarantee 99.95% uptime for the dedicated pool. If they want a 24-month term we can offer 5% cap.

Attachment: redline_sla_qv_draft.docx (redline of SLA template)

— Marissa
Head of Contracts & Customer Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@quantivis.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA ask — moving forward (pilot request)

Soojin / Aditya / Marissa — thanks for the thorough breakdown and the redline. Quantivis board sign-off is contingent on a clearer credit cap that doesn't expose us to outsized refunds in a production incident — the 6% for a 12-month committed dedicated pool is promising. A few confirmations before we proceed:

1) Pilot: we're open to the proposed 1-month dedicated pilot. During pilot we expect the 99.95% target and token-level traces enabled so our SREs can validate latency numbers.
2) Cap: we'd like the cap set at 8% for the pilot month (as a temporary compromise) and then 6% for the remainder of the 12-month term, provided observability requirements are met.
3) Maintenance windows: 4 hours/month for the dedicated pool is acceptable; please commit to scheduling outside our 09:00–18:00 PDT window unless urgent.
4) Pro-rata: we accept minute-granularity for partial months; request a short clause that ensures any credit payout for the pilot month will not exceed the pilot cap (8%).

If you can confirm those points and send a short term sheet + pilot operational runbook we will route to legal and finance. Also, is there a simple DocuSign link you can share for the pilot agreement?

Best,
Marta
